web.markdown:
![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g17/2018_hokuriku_01.jpg)

The Hokuriku Shinkansen (北陸新幹線) is a [shinkansen](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2018.html) line that connects [Tokyo](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2164.html) with [Tsuruga](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6650.html) in [Fukui Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1223.html). It is operated by the East Japan Railway Company, commonly known as JR East, and the West Japan Railway Company, commonly known as JR West.

The shinkansen line was opened as far as [Nagano](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6000.html) in 1997 in time for the Nagano Winter Olympics, extended to [Kanazawa](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2167.html) in 2015, and further extended to [Tsuruga](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6650.html) in 2024. Before its extension to Kanazawa, the line was popularly known as Nagano Shinkansen. The line is planned to be further extended to [Kyoto](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2158.html) and [Osaka](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2157.html) in the 2040s.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g24/2018_nagano_01_2403.gif)

The **Kagayaki** is the fastest train category along the Hokuriku Shinkansen, operating only in the mornings, late afternoons and evenings. While some operate all the way between [Tokyo](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2164.html) and [Tsuruga](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6650.html), others operate only between Tokyo and [Kanazawa](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2167.html). The Kagayaki stops only at major stations and features twelve cars, one of which is Gran Class, the first class service by JR. The Kagayaki is one of the few shinkansen trains without non-reserved seating. A seat reservation is mandatory. When all seats are booked out, standing tickets can be purchased.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g24/2018_nagano_03_2403.gif)

The **Hakutaka** is the slower of the two train categories that run along the entire length of the Hokuriku Shinkansen. It skips many stations between Tokyo and Nagano, but stops at most of the stations beyond Nagano. The Hakutaka features the same train sets as the Kagayaki, but it does offer non-reserved seating.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g24/2018_nagano_04_2403.gif)

The **Asama**, named after the large active volcano on the border between [Gunma Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1209.html) and [Nagano Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1216.html), runs just between Tokyo and Nagano.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g23/2018_nagano_05_2303.gif)

Also named after a famous mountain, **Tsurugi** trains operate between [Tsuruga](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6650.html) and [Toyama](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7500.html) stations, although a few operate only between Tsuruga and [Kanazawa](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2167.html). Stopping patterns vary by train, but a majority of trains stop at all stations.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g24/2018_nagano_06_2403.gif)

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g3/2018_legend_tohoku.gif)

Note: For simplification, some rare train compositions and stopping patterns are omitted.

**Questions?** Ask in our [forum](https://www.japan-guide.com/forum/quedisplay.html).

web.markdown:
Your JR tickets Just a click away

[Book Now](https://www.jrailpass.com/the-japan-rail-pass "Japan Rail Pass")

![Kagayaki Train in the Hokuriku Shinkansen Line](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/kagayaki-train-shinkansen.jpg)

The Hokuriku Shinkansen line is an extension of the Nagano Shinkansen line. Since 2015, it has offered a **quick and easy way to travel** from [Tokyo to Kanazawa](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/kanazawa-travel-guide).

You can use your [JR Pass](https://www.jrailpass.com/) on the Hokuriku Shinkansen line to **visit Kanazawa’s top attractions**, including the Kenrokuen Garden, Ninjadera Temple, Oyama Shrine, Omicho Market, and the Nagamachi samurai district.

The Hokuriku Shinkansen line also **extends from Kanazawa to Tsuruga**, taking just over 3 hours from Tokyo.

Below, you can find all the information you need to **plan a journey on the Hokuriku Shinkansen** with your JR Pass or one of the [regional passes](https://www.jrailpass.com/regional-passes).

Table of Contents \[ [hide](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#)\]

- [1 Hokuriku Shinkansen Map and Route](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#Hokuriku_Shinkansen_Map_and_Route)
- [2 Hokuriku Shinkansen Stops](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#Hokuriku_Shinkansen_Stops)
- [3 Hokuriku Shinkansen Bullet Train Services](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#Hokuriku_Shinkansen_Bullet_Train_Services)
  - [3.1 Kagayaki Shinkansen](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#Kagayaki_Shinkansen)
  - [3.2 Hakutaka Shinkansen](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#Hakutaka_Shinkansen)
  - [3.3 Asama Shinkansen](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#Asama_Shinkansen)
  - [3.4 Tsurugi Shinkansen](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#Tsurugi_Shinkansen)
- [4 Hokuriku Shinkansen Timetable](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#Hokuriku_Shinkansen_Timetable)
- [5 Hokuriku Shinkansen Ticket Prices](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#Hokuriku_Shinkansen_Ticket_Prices)
- [6 Tokyo to Kanazawa by Hokuriku Shinkansen](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#Tokyo_to_Kanazawa_by_Hokuriku_Shinkansen)
- [7 JR Pass for Hokuriku Shinkansen](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/hokuriku-shinkansen-jr-pass#JR_Pass_for_Hokuriku_Shinkansen)

## Hokuriku Shinkansen Map and Route

Below is a map showing the Hokuriku Shinkansen line and the different routes you can take, depending on your travel plans.

![Hokuriku Shinkansen Line Map](https://www.jrailpass.com/images/shinkansen-bullet-trains/hokuriku-shinkansen/Hokuriku-shinkansen-line.svg)The Hokuriku Shinkansen Line Map

## Hokuriku Shinkansen Stops

The main stations along the Hokuriku Shinkansen line are **[Tokyo Station](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/tokyo-train-station), Nagano Station, and Kanazawa Station**.

Additional stations along this line include:

- Ueno
- Omiya
- Kumagaya
- Honjowaseda
- Takasaki
- Annakaharuna
- Karuizawa
- Sakudaira
- Ueda
- Iiyama
- Joetsumyoko
- Itoigawa
- Kurobe-Unazuki Onsen
- Toyama
- Shin-Takaoka
- Komatsu
- Kaga Onsen
- Awara Onsen
- Fukui
- Echizen-Takefu
- Tsuruga

If you wish to bypass the smaller stations along your route, **consider reserving a seat on the Kagayaki express train**. The Hakutaka also bypasses many stations between Tokyo and Nagano.

## Hokuriku Shinkansen Bullet Train Services

You can use the Hokuriku Shinkansen to travel to **Nagano, Kanazawa, Toyama, and a number of other destinations**.

### **Kagayaki Shinkansen**

**Stops**: Tokyo – Ueno – Omiya – Nagano – Toyama – Kanazawa – Komatsu – Kaga Onsen – Awara Onsen – Fukui – Echizen-Takefu – Tsuruga

**The Kagayaki is the fastest train** on the Hokuriku Shinkansen line. This train stops from Tokyo to Kanazawa in Ueno Station, Omiya Station, Nagano Station and Toyama Station.

The journey from Tokyo to Kanazawa will take you **less than 2.5 hours**. The train operates at 260 km/h (160mph). The Kagayaki features only reserved seats, in both its green class and the luxury [Gran Class](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/shinkansen-gran-class) cars.

![Kagayaki Seat reservation](https://www.jrailpass.com/images/shinkansen-bullet-trains/hokuriku-shinkansen/Kagayaki-seat-reservation.png)

### **Hakutaka** **Shinkansen**

**Stops**: Tokyo – Ueno – Omiya – Takasaki – Karuizawa – Sakadaira – Ueda – Nagano – Iiyama – Joetsu-Myoko – Itoigawa – Kurobe-Unazukionsen – Toyama – Shin-Takaoka – Kanazawa – Komatsu – Kaga Onsen – Awara Onsen – Fukui – Echizen-Takefu – Tsuruga

Hakutaka **makes more stops between Tokyo and Kanazawa** than the Kagayaki (less than 3 hours). The operating speed of Hakutaka is 260 km/h (160 mph).

About 1 in 3 Hakutaka trains **travels all the way to Tsuruga**. They stop at every station along the route from Kanazawa to Tsuruga.

![Hakutaka Seat reservation](https://www.jrailpass.com/images/shinkansen-bullet-trains/hokuriku-shinkansen/Hakutaka-seat-reservation.png)

### **Asama Shinkansen**

**Stops**: Tokyo – Ueno – Omiya – Takasaki – Karuizawa – Sakudaira – Ueda – Nagano

The Asama **takes its name from Mount Asama**, an active volcano near Karuizawa.

Two train types operate the Asama train services: **8-coach and 12-coach train sets**. Both are non-smoking trains with reserved and non-reserved seating space, Green Cars, and wheelchair space.

![Asama Seat reservation](https://www.jrailpass.com/images/shinkansen-bullet-trains/hokuriku-shinkansen/Asama-seat-reservation.png)

### **Tsurugi Shinkansen**

**Stops**: Toyama – Shin-Takaoka – Kanazawa – Komatsu – Kaga Onsen – Awara Onsen – Fukui – Echizen-Takefu – Tsuruga

The Tsurugi train serves as the **main connection between Toyama and Kanazawa**. The Tsurugi uses 12-coach trains, 3 of which are not in use currently. 1 of the 12 cars is a Green Car (first class).

The majority of Tsurugi trains run between Toyama and Tsuruga, with a small number running **just between Kanazawa and Tsuruga**.

Most trains stop at every station, but **stopping patterns vary by train**.

![Tsurugi Seat reservation](https://www.jrailpass.com/images/shinkansen-bullet-trains/hokuriku-shinkansen/Tsurugi-seat-reservation.png)

[Buy your JR Pass](https://www.jrailpass.com/the-japan-rail-pass)

## Hokuriku Shinkansen Timetable

The first train of the day leaves Tokyo for Tsuruga at **around 6:15 a.m**. The last train of the day departs for Kanazawa at about 9:00 p.m.

Hokuriku Shinkansen trains run roughly **every 20 to 40 minutes** during peak hours, with reduced frequency at other times of the day.

Schedules are similar for the return journey from Tsuruga or Kanazawa to Tokyo. For full details, you can check the [Navitime travel planner](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/).

## Hokuriku Shinkansen Ticket Prices

Below is an overview of ticket prices doe the Hokuriku Shinkansen line.

|     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Route** | **Ordinary Unreserved Seat** | **Ordinary Reserved Seat** | **Green Car (1st Class)** |
| **Tokyo → Tsuruga** | ¥18,560 | ¥18,890 | ¥26,740 |
| **Tokyo → Kanazawa** | ¥16,580 | ¥16,910 | ¥23,370 |
| **Tokyo → Nagano** | ¥10,540 | ¥10,870 | ¥14,530 |
| **Nagano → Kanazawa** | ¥11,320 | ¥11,650 | ¥15,220 |
| **Kanazawa → Tsuruga** | ¥7,680 | ¥8,010 | ¥10,280 |

## Tokyo to Kanazawa by Hokuriku Shinkansen

From either Tokyo Station or Nagano Station, you can take the express train **Kagayaki or the Hakutaka to Kanazawa Station**. The Kagayaki typically departs during morning and evening hours.

The trip from [Tokyo to Kanazawa](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/kanazawa-travel-guide) takes only **2.5 hours on the express train** or about 3 to 3.5 hours on the non-express train.

If using this train, **make your seat reservations in advance**. If all seats are booked, standing tickets can be purchased.

**An additional train called the Tsurugi** operates on this line between Kanazawa Station and Toyama Station. The Tsurugi trains do not connect to Tokyo or Nagano and cater mostly to local traffic commuting between the 2 cities.

## JR Pass for Hokuriku Shinkansen

Passage on the Hokuriku Shinkansen is **covered by the Japan Rail Pass**, as well as [Hokuriku Arch Pass](https://www.jrailpass.com/regional-passes/hokuriku-arch-pass).

You can [activate your JR Pass](https://www.jrailpass.com/faq/japan-rail-pass-exchange-offices) in **many train stations**, including the Travel Service Centers in Nagano and [Tokyo Station](https://www.jrailpass.com/blog/tokyo-train-station), and the Nippon Travel Agency branch at Kanazawa Station.

If you wish to make a [seat reservation](https://www.jrailpass.com/faq/seat-reservation), **visit a ticketing office** within the train station. Give the staff member your desired destination and present your JR Pass.

Once you have your [JR Pass](https://www.jrailpass.com/the-japan-rail-pass) in hand, you’re ready to travel on the Hokuriku Shinkansen line!
